title: Group employees by department but return the result as a `TreeMap` so the department keys are sorted alphabetically, using the three-argument `Collectors.groupingBy`. Explain how to choose the map implementation and the downstream collector.
shortTitle: Group employees by department into a sorted TreeMap using groupingBy with a map supplier
keyPoints: The three-argument `groupingBy(classifier, mapFactory, downstream)` lets you pick both the map type and how each group is reduced.
Passing `TreeMap::new` as the map factory returns keys sorted by natural order, instead of the unordered default `HashMap`.
The one-argument form returns `Map<K, List<T>>` backed by a `HashMap` with no key order.
The downstream collector (for example `toList`, `counting`, `mapping`) decides what each group's value becomes.
A custom key order comes from `() -> new TreeMap<>(comparator)` as the map factory.
`LinkedHashMap::new` preserves the encounter order of the first appearance of each key.
Sorting the keys via the map factory needs no separate sort step, unlike sorting a `HashMap`'s entries afterward.

s1_definition.oneliner: `groupingBy(classifier, TreeMap::new, downstream)` groups into a map whose keys stay sorted, instead of the unordered default `HashMap`.
s1_definition.profdef:
The three-argument `Collectors.groupingBy` has three independent parts.

- **classifier** – a function that extracts the grouping key from each element, for example `Employee::getDepartment`.
- **map factory** – a supplier that creates the result map, for example `TreeMap::new` for sorted keys or `LinkedHashMap::new` for insertion order.
- **downstream collector** – reduces each group's elements into the map value, for example `toList()`, `counting()`, or `mapping(...)`.
- **default form** – the one-argument `groupingBy` uses a `HashMap` and `toList`, giving no key order.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya sorts employee files into labelled trays by department. The ordinary way throws the trays onto the shelf in no particular order (a `HashMap`). The sorted way (a `TreeMap`) keeps the trays in alphabetical order by department label, so Risk always sits after Management without her rearranging anything.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  groupingBy(classifier, mapFactory, downstream)

  elements
     │  classifier: Employee::getDepartment
     ▼
  ┌──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
  │  Management  │    Risk      │   Trading     │   <- keys
  │  [Pankaj]    │   [Priya]    │  [Rajesh]     │   <- downstream toList()
  └──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────┘
     │  mapFactory: TreeMap::new  ->  keys kept sorted
     ▼
  { Management=[...], Risk=[...], Trading=[...] }
```

```text
  Map factory decides key order

  ┌───────────────┬───────────────────────────┐
  │ HashMap::new  │  Trading, Risk, Management │  (unspecified)
  ├───────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
  │ TreeMap::new  │  Management, Risk, Trading │  (natural sort)
  ├───────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
  │ TreeMap(cmp)  │  Trading, Risk, Management │  (reverse)
  ├───────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
  │ LinkedHashMap │  first-seen insertion order│
  └───────────────┴───────────────────────────┘
```

```text
  Downstream collector shapes the VALUE

  toList()      -> Map<Dept, List<Employee>>
  counting()    -> Map<Dept, Long>
  mapping(name) -> Map<Dept, List<String>>
  averaging()   -> Map<Dept, Double>
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
`groupingBy` has three overloads, and the three-argument form is the one I reach for when I care about the type and ordering of the result map. It takes the classifier that decides the key, a map factory that chooses the map implementation, and a downstream collector that reduces each group. By passing `TreeMap::new` as the factory I get a map whose department keys stay sorted in natural order, instead of the arbitrary order of the default `HashMap`.

In my banking work at the National Bank of India the org-chart screen grouped employees by department and had to show departments alphabetically so the page looked the same on every load. I used `groupingBy` with the department as the classifier, `TreeMap::new` as the factory, and a `mapping` downstream that collected just the employee names, and the result came out already sorted by department with no separate sort step.

The senior point I always add is that the map factory is a deliberate design choice. `TreeMap` gives sorted keys and can take a custom comparator, `LinkedHashMap` preserves the order in which keys first appear, and the default `HashMap` gives the best throughput when order does not matter. Because the downstream collector is fully composable, I can combine sorted keys with counting, averaging, or mapping in the same call. The one gotcha I watch for is a null key, which a `TreeMap` rejects, so I normalize the classifier to a safe default first.

Think of Priya filing employee folders into labelled trays: the `TreeMap` keeps those trays alphabetical on the shelf automatically, so Management always sits before Risk before Trading.

Remember one sentence: the three-argument `groupingBy` lets you pick the map type with a factory like `TreeMap::new` for sorted keys and the downstream collector for each group's value.
